text: IPDE – Instrumentation Project and Document Engineering
A practical guide to selection, mounting, wiring and commissioning

alt: Illustration of a radar level sensor on an industrial tank

text: Cover image generated for this presentation. Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
A level sensor tells the control system how much material a vessel contains
The height or presence of liquid, slurry or bulk solid inside a tank, silo or vessel.
The reading can protect equipment, control filling and maintain inventory.
A sensor needs a clear, representative measurement point.
Poor mounting can create false echoes, blocked probes or drift.
Commissioning links the physical level to a useful signal for PLC, alarm or display.
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
Choose the task before choosing the technology
A switch changes state at a fixed height.
A transmitter reports the actual level across a range.
A common installation uses both: a continuous transmitter for control and an independent switch for safety alarm.
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
Select a method that matches the medium and the vessel
Guided-wave radar and capacitance probes are also widely used where contact measurement suits the process.
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
Record process information before issuing the instrument specification
Liquid, slurry, foam, powder or granules
Temperature, pressure, density, conductivity and vapour
Height, geometry, nozzles, agitators, coils and ladders
Alarm, inventory, control, interface or pump protection
Hazardous area, hygiene, access, cable route and power
Use the manufacturer’s installation manual and the plant’s safety procedure as controlling documents.
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
Plan the work, mount correctly, then prove the measurement
Apply permit, isolation, lockout and vessel access controls.
Confirm nozzle, clear path, orientation and service access.
Fit the sensor, gasket, process seal and support as specified.
Use the wiring diagram, grounding method and approved cable entry.
Enter range values, test alarms and update loop records.
Hold point: do not energize a device until the mechanical installation and hazardous-area checks are complete.
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
The process connection and sensing path determine measurement quality
Mount away from inlet streams, walls and internal obstructions. Keep the beam path clear.
Place at a representative low point. Protect the cable and account for density changes.
Keep clear of turbulence and product build-up. Provide clearance for the moving or sensing element.
Avoid mounting directly above a fill stream unless the manufacturer confirms that the design handles it.
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
Treat configuration as part of installation, not as a separate afterthought
Match supply voltage, signal type and cable shielding to the datasheet.
Bond metallic parts where required. Maintain IP rating with suitable glands and plugs.
Set empty and full reference points. Enter tank geometry only when the application needs volume.
Simulate level changes or use a known reference. Verify display, PLC value and alarm action.
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
Level instruments support safe and efficient plant operation
Wet-well control, pump protection and overflow alarm
Corrosion-resistant measurement in reactors and storage tanks
Inventory measurement and independent overfill protection
Silo monitoring for powders, grains and pellets
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
A dependable level measurement starts with a correct application choice and ends with a documented loop test.
Select the sensing principle for the medium and duty
Mount at a representative point with a clear sensing path
Follow the approved mechanical and electrical instructions
Verify range, alarms and PLC indication before handover
Sources: Endress+Hauser, Level measurement overview and Continuous level measurement guidance, accessed 11 Nov 2026; VEGA Field Service Pro Tips, accessed 11 Nov 2026.
